outcome: removal of retained products of conception (RPOC)
patient symptoms (pelvic pain, abnormal vaginal bleeding)
cohort: A 34-year-old patient experiencing abnormal vaginal bleeding and persistent pelvic pain three months after a caesarean section, diagnosed with an isthmic uterine niche within a caesarean scar area containing a poorly vascularised heterogeneous hyperechoic focal mass.
finding: The combined hysteroscopic and laparoscopic approach effectively removed retained placental tissue and corrected the uterine wall defect without complications, leading to a reconstituted uterine wall and asymptomatic status at 3 months.
mod_finding: The study describes a treatment for a uterine scar defect (isthmocele) and retained products of conception, which is an uncommon occurrence following caesarean section, thereby addressing a complication directly related to the mode of birth.
